title: Find All Duplicates in an Array
notes:
Task: Return every value that occurs twice in an array of values from 1 through n.
Idea: Use each value as an index and negate the indexed slot to mark its first occurrence.
Invariant: A negative slot means the corresponding value has already been encountered.
Edge cases: The input is modified in place; each value appears at most twice under the problem constraints.
complexity_reason: Each value performs one indexed check and possible sign change.

title: Find All Duplicates in an Array
notes:
Task: Find values appearing twice while using constant extra space.
Idea: Negate the slot for each value's index on its first occurrence; a negative slot on another occurrence marks a duplicate.
Invariant: The sign at index value-1 records whether that value has been seen.
Edge cases: Use abs when reading a value because its own slot may already have been negated.
complexity_reason: The array is scanned once and no input-sized auxiliary structure is created.

title: String Compression
notes:
Task: Compress consecutive character runs in place and return the length of the compressed prefix.
Idea: Use a read pointer to find each run and a write pointer to store the character and count digits.
Invariant: chars[:write] contains the compressed representation of all runs already processed.
Edge cases: A count of one is omitted; multi-digit run lengths are written one digit at a time.
complexity_reason: Read and write pointers traverse the array linearly and no auxiliary array is allocated.

title: String Compression
notes:
Task: Write run-length compression into the original character array and return its new length.
Idea: Scan each run, write its character, then write decimal digits of its count if greater than one.
Invariant: The prefix before write is the compressed encoding of the processed input prefix.
Edge cases: Counts may have multiple digits; the method mutates chars and returns the valid prefix length.
complexity_reason: Each input character is scanned once and output is written in place.

title: Add Two Numbers II
notes:
Task: Add two numbers whose linked-list digits are stored from most significant to least significant.
Idea: Push both digit sequences onto stacks and add from the least significant end, prepending result digits.
Invariant: carry represents the overflow from the digits processed from right to left.
Edge cases: Unequal list lengths are handled by empty-stack checks; Node is supplied by the judge.
complexity_reason: Both lists are traversed into stacks and each digit is processed once.

title: Add Two Numbers II
notes:
Task: Add two forward-order linked-list numbers and return the sum in forward order.
Idea: Push digits onto stacks, add popped digits with carry, and prepend each result digit.
Invariant: The result list is the correctly ordered sum suffix for the digits processed so far.
Edge cases: Missing digits contribute zero; ListNode is provided by the judge.
complexity_reason: The two stacks store all digits and each digit is popped once.

title: Arithmetic Slices II - Subsequence
notes:
Task: Count arithmetic subsequences of length at least three.
Idea: For each ending index i, map each difference to the number of subsequences of length at least two ending at i with that difference.
Invariant: Extending dp[j][diff] by nums[i] creates that many new valid length-at-least-three subsequences.
Edge cases: Use wide integer differences because subtracting extreme values can exceed a 32-bit range.
complexity_reason: Every index pair contributes one difference-state transition.

title: Arithmetic Slices II - Subsequence
notes:
Task: Count arithmetic subsequences of length at least three, not necessarily contiguous.
Idea: Store counts by ending index and difference, extending every earlier pair's arithmetic subsequences.
Invariant: dp[i][d] counts arithmetic subsequences of length at least two ending at i with difference d; only existing sequences contribute to the answer.
Edge cases: Use long for differences so subtraction does not overflow 32-bit integers.
complexity_reason: The nested loops process every pair and each map operation is expected constant time.

title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
notes:
Task: Return all values in [1,n] missing from an array of length n.
Idea: Negate the array slot corresponding to every encountered value; positive slots at the end indicate missing values.
Invariant: A negative slot means its one-based index appeared in the input.
Edge cases: Use abs before indexing because a slot may already be negative; the array is modified in place.
complexity_reason: The array is scanned for marking and once more to collect missing indices.

title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
notes:
Task: Find values from 1 through n that do not occur in the input.
Idea: Mark each encountered value's index negative, then report indices that remain positive.
Invariant: A negative value at index i means value i+1 was present.
Edge cases: Apply abs when indexing and marking; the input array is modified.
complexity_reason: Two linear scans are used with no additional input-sized structure.

title: Delete Node in a BST
notes:
Task: Delete the node with key from a binary search tree while preserving BST ordering.
Idea: Recurse toward the key; for a node with two children, copy its inorder successor value and delete that successor from the right subtree.
Invariant: Each recursive result is a valid BST containing the original subtree minus the deleted key.
Edge cases: Missing keys leave the tree unchanged; TreeNode is supplied by the judge.
complexity_reason: The search and successor deletion follow paths bounded by tree height.

title: Delete Node in a BST
notes:
Task: Remove a target key from a BST and return the new subtree root.
Idea: Search by key; if two children exist, replace the node with the minimum value in its right subtree and delete that successor.
Invariant: The returned subtree remains ordered and excludes the target key.
Edge cases: Nodes with zero or one child are replaced directly; TreeNode is judge-provided.
complexity_reason: The recursive search and successor removal traverse at most tree-height paths.

title: Sort Characters By Frequency
notes:
Task: Reorder characters by descending occurrence frequency.
Idea: Count characters and sort distinct characters by their counts, emitting each character the counted number of times.
Invariant: Output groups are ordered by nonincreasing character frequency.
Edge cases: Any order among characters with equal frequency is valid; empty input returns an empty string.
complexity_reason: Counting is linear, then u distinct characters are sorted and expanded into output.

title: Sort Characters By Frequency
notes:
Task: Sort a string's characters in descending frequency order.
Idea: Count characters and sort the distinct character entries by count before appending repeated characters.
Invariant: The output appends every character exactly its original frequency.
Edge cases: Equal-frequency character order is unspecified; the frequency map stores only characters present in s.
complexity_reason: The algorithm counts n characters, sorts u distinct characters, and emits n output characters.

title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
notes:
Task: Find the minimum number of arrows needed to intersect every balloon interval.
Idea: Sort by right endpoint and fire an arrow at the earliest finishing endpoint; reuse it for every interval containing that point.
Invariant: end is the position of the most recent arrow and all processed intervals are already burst.
Edge cases: An interval starting at end is burst by the same arrow because endpoints are inclusive.
complexity_reason: Sorting dominates the single greedy scan.

title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
notes:
Task: Minimize arrows that each burst all intervals containing their horizontal position.
Idea: Sort by end coordinate and place an arrow at the end of the first unburst interval.
Invariant: Each chosen arrow bursts every subsequent interval whose start is no greater than the arrow coordinate.
Edge cases: Empty input needs zero arrows; intervals include both endpoints.
complexity_reason: The interval sort takes O(n log n) time and the scan is linear.

title: Minimum Moves to Equal Array Elements
notes:
Task: Minimize moves when one move increments n-1 array elements by one.
Idea: Treat each move as decrementing the one excluded element; reduce every value to the array minimum.
Invariant: The required moves for value x are x-minimum, so their sum is the total number of moves.
Edge cases: Empty arrays are outside the problem constraints; negative values are also handled by the difference formula.
complexity_reason: Finding the minimum and summing differences each scan the array once.

title: Minimum Moves to Equal Array Elements
notes:
Task: Compute the minimum number of moves to make all array values equal by incrementing n-1 values per move.
Idea: Equivalently decrement one element per move until all values equal the minimum.
Invariant: The answer is the sum of each value's difference from the minimum.
Edge cases: The array is nonempty under the problem constraints; use a wide accumulator for the total.
complexity_reason: Two linear passes find the minimum and accumulate differences.

title: 4Sum II
notes:
Task: Count index tuples whose four array values sum to zero.
Idea: Count all pair sums from A and B, then look up the opposite sum for each pair from C and D.
Invariant: sums[x] is the number of index pairs from the first two arrays with sum x.
Edge cases: Duplicate values and repeated sums count as distinct index combinations.
complexity_reason: The algorithm enumerates pair sums for each of two array pairs and stores one side's counts.

title: 4Sum II
notes:
Task: Count quadruples with one value from each array whose sum is zero.
Idea: Store frequencies of A+B sums and add the frequency of -(C+D) for each pair from the other two arrays.
Invariant: Each map entry counts all index pairs that produce its sum.
Edge cases: The count may be large, so use a long accumulator for the number of quadruples.
complexity_reason: Both pair loops perform O(n^2) work and the map stores pair-sum frequencies.
